history.dynasty: Deva Dynasty of Sribhumi (Samatata); pilgrim inscription of Sri Jayadeva 11th-12th c. CE
history.period: 7th-9th centuries CE (bas-relief style; 'if not earlier' per Tripura Tourism)
history.summary: SOLID ENTRY. Unakoti ('one less than a crore') is Tripura's most famous Shaivite rock-cut pilgrimage site, ~8 km from Kailashahar in Unakoti district (a UNESCO World Heritage tentative-list site since 2022). The bas-relief sculptures, patronised by the Deva Dynasty of Sribhumi in Samatata, date to the 7th-9th centuries CE on stylistic grounds; the only inscription is an 11th-12th-century Bengali-script record of a pilgrim named Sri Jayadeva. The centrepiece is the ~30-ft-high Unakotiswara Kal Bhairava Shiva head with a 10-ft embroidered headdress, flanked by a Durga-on-lion figure and another female figure, plus three enormous half-buried Nandi bulls and gigantic Ganesha figures. Legend: Shiva, travelling to Kashi with one crore gods and goddesses, halted here; all but Shiva failed to wake at dawn, and his curse turned them to stone - hence 'one less than a crore'. CSV town 'Kailashahar' is CORRECT (nearest town, ~8 km). town_description: Kailashahar is the headquarters of Unakoti district, Tripura, on the Manu river ~178 km from Agartala. Unakoti's forested rock-cut complex with waterfalls is the district's prime tourist spot and a major Shaivite pilgrimage centre, maintained by the state with an annual Ashokastami fair.
